text:
maria: Heads-up — sketching an auxiliary traffic shaper idea to sit after ingress but before admission. Goal: isolate greedy tenants' short bursts without changing long-term fairness logic. Thoughts? :thinking:

kevin: Sounds interesting. Do you mean a lightweight per-tenant leaky-bucket that can pre-warm/queue bursts? How does this differ from soft-lease right now?

maria: Exactly a leaky-bucket-ish frontdoor. Difference: it's stateless-ish (token counters in memcache) and tuned only for short windows (<30s) to avoid interfering with reservoir logic. Admission still enforces SLA/backpressure.

sam: Can we get a diagram and interface sketch? We need to know signals it emits for the admission layer (e.g., 'burst_dampened', 'queued', 'drop'). Also need metrics: burst_count, hold_time_ms, qdepth.

maria: Yep drafting an RFC, will add a minimal protobuf for signals. Sketch will have: ingress -> shaper -> admission -> router. Shaper returns 200 + header X-Shaper-Status:[ok|delayed|shed].

kevin: Example header/payload? I can mock a shim:
```json
{"tenant_id":"t-123","shaper_status":"delayed","delay_ms":120}
```

raj: Important: integrate abuse signals (rate-of-change, repeated patterns) so shaper can bump a penalty factor. Also avoid using shaper as a fingerprinting surface for timing attacks.

lina: ML note: any scoring (abuse prob) must be async and heavily cached — we can't add 50ms sync latency. Maybe shaper consults a cached score bucket with TTL 5s.

sam: Ops concerns: memcache hot keys, TTL churn. Let's use a hashed slot with bounded fanout and per-slot counters instead of per-tenant keys for very large tenant counts.

maria: Agreed. Tradeoff doc: per-tenant exact counters vs. approximate sketch (count-min). We'll prefer approximate when tenant_count > 100k and fall back to exact for top X tenants.

throttle-bot: Auto: created RFC draft: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/auxiliary-shaper-draft — assigned to @maria, reviewers @kevin @sam @raj

maria: Action items: I'll add interface proto + metrics list, plan a teardown test harness (synthetic burst profiles), and run a 2-week dogfood on dev cluster. PTAL on RFC.

kevin: Ack. I'll prototype the shim in ingress-gateway and try to keep memcache-only state so private deployments can opt out easily.

sam: If we can keep fallback behavior predictable (header present but no enforcement), we can roll out as opt-in canary.

maria: Cool, thanks. Meeting later? 3pm PT to walk through numbers.

kevin: I'll be there. :+1:
